notes:
Summary: Sienna Lattice builds low-latency inference for market signal personalization across mobile and web. High sensitivity to both P95 latency and per-token cost — trading UX depends on sub-100ms response windows for micro-interactions. Team is convinced caching + batching + quantization are primary levers; wants Redwood Optimize help and Dedicated/private deployment options for data residency.

Key constraints / asks (from CTO Ari Vasquez and infra lead Priya Rao):
- Latency target: <= 60-100ms P95 for 16-32 token generation on live traffic (~70% short responses).
- Throughput target: sustained 400-800 QPS during market hours; spiky bursts to 2k QPS for major events.
- Cost goal: reduce per-1k-token cost by 30-50% vs current vendor over a 6-month window.
- Security: must run inside VPC for production, SSO + audit logs mandatory, KMS integration required. Data residency: US only.
- Model preferences: open model family (Llama/Redwood-verified candidates) with willingness to test quantized variants (int8/int4) if quality regression under 3% on eval set.
- Routing/fallback: need automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized model for non-critical requests and to a multi-region replica for DR.

POC scope (agreed on 2026-03-05 call):
1) Baseline perf: Redwood runs baseline on their hosted/dedicated test pool using customer sample prompts (drive:benchmark-prompts.csv). Measure P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization.
2) Batching experiments: test continuous batching windows (5-25ms) and dynamic batching heuristics to hit latency SLOs while maximizing throughput.
3) KV-prefix caching: measure hit rate impact on end-to-end latency for repeated prompts, integrate with user session keys.
4) Quantization sweep: int8 -> int4 on selected model family; run quality regressions against Sienna's business eval set (sensitive false-positive cases flagged).
5) Cost model: Redwood to produce per-route cost model showing unit economics with/without batching/caching/quantization.

Notes from meetings / timeline: 
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (Maya + Ari). High-level product fit; Sienna sent sample prompts. (linked_fireflies: ff_20260115_2201)
- 2026-02-20: Technical deep-dive with SE (Liam). Discussed current infra (on-prem GPU pool + cloud fallback), asked about smart routing and observability hooks. (ff_20260220_3341)
- 2026-03-05: Procurement/ops call. Agreed POC scope and timeline. Sienna requested benchmarking templates and Redwood to provide dedicated test pool credentials. (ff_20260305_9872)

Quotes / call snippets: 
- "If we can't hit ~75ms P95 for small responses, the feature will feel sluggish to traders." — Ari (CTO)
- "We can tolerate a 2-3% model quality drop for non-critical personalization if cost savings are substantial, but not for compliance-critical signals." — Priya (Infra)

Risks / unknowns: 
- Need representative production traces — Sienna's sample prompts are small but tail behavior during market events unknown.
- Legal wants explicit data residency verification for private deployment.
- Procurement timeline tied to Q2 budget approval, could slip to May.

Action items / next steps: 
- Redwood: provision dedicated test pool + shared runbook for perf tests. Deliver initial baseline report by 2026-03-19.
- Sienna: provide a labeled eval set highlighting safety/compliance-critical prompts and open test credentials for short-term traffic replay. (drive:benchmark-prompts.csv)
- SE (Liam) to run batching/caching matrix and present costs delta in POC wrap-up.

External refs: Pricing deck (drive:sienna/Redwood-POC-pricing-v1.pdf), Security FAQ (drive:sienna/security-faq-response.docx).

- Blocker: legal needs KMS attestation; link to SEC ticket SEC-88.
- Good fit for Redwood Optimize; heavy interest in quantization guidance.
